statement.p: Suppose that an accelerating car goes from 0 mph to 58.6 mph in five seconds. Its velocity is given in the following table, converted from miles per hour to feet per second, so that all time measurements are in seconds. (Note: 1 mph is 22/15 ft/sec.) solution.p: To measure the average acceleration over an interval, we calculate the average rate of change of velocity over the interval. The units of acceleration are ft/s per second, or ft/s/s, written ft/s{}^2. \mbox{average acceleration for } 0\le t\le 1 = \frac{\mbox{Change in velocity}}{\mbox{Change in time}}, so, reading the velocities from the table, we have \frac{v(1) - v(0)}{1} = 29.32 - 0.00 = 29.32 \mbox{ ft/s}{}^2. Similarly, \mbox{avg accel for } 1\le t\le 2 = \frac{v(2) - v(1)}{2-1} = 50.82 - 29.32 = 21.5 \mbox{ ft/s}{}^2.
